title: Cyberpunk interactive game I made. Not just a video but a playable game.
author: InfiniteCobbler2073
selftext:
Anyone wants to play?

I'm building a FMV-style cyberpunk thriller game.

The workflow so far:

* GPT Image 2 for visual direction, character/scene concepts, and key art style exploration
* Seedance 2.0 for generating cinematic video sequences
* Claude Code for prototyping and building the playable structure around the episodes

John Wick-style action with a Blade Runner 2049 mood.

A few episodes are already playable, and I'm working on more right now.

  
I'd love feedback from people interested in AI-assisted game development, especially around the FMV workflow, pacing, and how the generative video fits into interactive gameplay.

Leave comments or DM me to get a discord channel get in to play.

comments.author: s_a_m_12344
comments.body: It's.. , by playable you mean that you can click and x or Y video plays no? Cause there is nothing else playable there

comments.author: AwakeEnuf
comments.body:
Not sure why this got shown to me as I do follow the sub, but if you want honest feedback, this is absolutely what people mean by slop, it's the most generic looking "visual novel" kind of game imaginable, and although it might have been fun to make or something, this is literally not a game.

And I say this as a huge visual novel game fan.

comments.author: Southern_Charge5794
comments.body: I do like cyberpunk and AI to boost my productivity and it looks like low-effort game created in a few hours. My personal opinion that game should not be two prompts but hundreds of hours of effort
